key_insight: A model-free MITM adversary can progressively identify a closed-loop plant from intercepted input-output data and use the resulting behavioral model to synthesize covert reference-tracking attacks.
engineering_relevance: The framework exposes how residual-based intrusion detection can miss incremental system identification and subsequent manipulation of networked control systems.
method: Collect an initial rank-deficient Hankel matrix using low-amplitude probing within an analytical stealth bound.
Use rank-increasing experiments and causal predictor-based masking to reach behavioral rank n + mL in exactly n + mL − 1 steps.
Solve a DeePC-style optimization to track a desired reference while respecting the IDS constraint.
evidence_signal: DC motor simulations with PI control demonstrate full-rank identification and stealthy tracking; stealth is analytically guaranteed in Phases 1 and 3 but supported only numerically in Phase 2.
watch_item: The method assumes noise-free LTI dynamics, leaving robustness to measurement noise and model changes unresolved.
paper_title: Iterative Behavioral Identification for Covert Misappropriation Attacks
